summary: U.S. equity markets surged Wednesday after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, with the Dow jumping over 1,200 points and the S&P 500 rallying 1.75% by midday. Investors appear relieved by the prospect of divided government, betting that Democratic control will limit Trump administration policy volatility. The Reserve Bank of Australia hiked rates 25 basis points to 4.85% overnight, citing persistent inflation pressures, while Bitcoin rebounded above $80,000 despite three consecutive days of ETF outflows totaling $1.16 billion. Factory orders data came in stronger than expected at 1.8%, supporting optimism around industrial demand. Oil prices tumbled 7% on diplomatic progress, easing inflation concerns and boosting rate-sensitive sectors. The next major catalyst is Friday's October jobs report, with 65,000 payrolls expected and unemployment holding at 4.2%.

signals.title: Democrats sweep Congress, market rallies on divided government
signals.desc: Democrats won both House and Senate, sparking a 1,200-point Dow surge as investors price gridlock limiting policy uncertainty and AI regulation fears.

signals.title: Bitcoin reclaims $80,000 after three-day ETF outflow streak eases
signals.desc: BTC rebounded from $76,300 to above $80,000 as ETF outflows slowed from $643M to $116M, with institutional selling pressure moderating.

signals.title: RBA hikes rates 25bp to 4.85% as inflation remains sticky
signals.desc: Australia's central bank raised rates citing capacity pressures and fuel price pass-through, signaling persistent global inflation challenges.

signals.title: Factory orders beat at 1.8% vs. 1.1% consensus
signals.desc: September factory orders topped estimates, reinforcing resilient industrial demand and supporting cyclical equity exposure ahead of jobs data.

signals.title: Oil crashes 7% on diplomatic progress, election outcome
signals.desc: WTI crude fell sharply toward $95 as geopolitical tensions eased and Democratic sweep reduces odds of aggressive energy policy, pressuring XLE.

verdict: Risk assets rallying on election clarity and easing oil prices, but Friday's jobs data and persistent central bank hawkishness keep volatility elevated.
